relevant_prose: §12.6.4.4 defines source, target, current document and recursive nested /T navigation; each intermediate target becomes current. Its NOTE says an infinite cycle is an error and interactive PDF processors need to attempt detection and refuse execution if found.
§12.3.2.2 says explicit GoToR/GoToE page operands use zero-based integer indexes in the target; corrected text includes embedded Go-To.
EC3 Issue #256 generalizes §12.6.4.8 /Base to all relative URIs in a PDF, supporting Table 204 /F URL interpretation; this is already exercised in actions.rs.

features.obligations: S required /GoToR; F required target file spec; D required (Name, byte string, or explicit array); explicit array uses target document zero-based page integer; optional PDF2 SD array identifies target structure element and should precede D; NewWindow is optional and absent policy is left to processor preference.

Array page index is distinguished by a four-page target. SD conflicts with D and resolves only in target page 2. Cross-document destination geometry test fails for zoom/coordinates (B23).
features.verdict: Table file request, zero-based target page, SD precedence and host window path have discriminating assertions. Existing remote and embedded view tests still fail: target page is selected but /XYZ scale and position are dropped after Supply; this is existing B23, not a new finding.
features.residuals: Remote named destinations were absent from the existing action integration tests, although destination.rs tests exercise each destination syntax locally and the live remote array/SD controls pass. A scratch exact-xref candidate now drives Table203 Name and byte-string /D values through the public remote Supply path with distinct target NameTree/Dests tables, a remote target page index 2, and an explicit-array control. It does not create a same-key collision and cannot resolve B08; parent should decide whether the additional target-context proof is worth integration.

features.obligations: S required /GoToE; F optional root relative to source root; D required destination in target; NewWindow optional with should-level semantics; T optional when F exists and otherwise required. A missing T with present F means the supplied root itself is the target.
features.assertions: embedded_go_to.rs::a_root_document_the_action_names_is_asked_of_the_host; ::a_supplied_root_resumes_the_walk_and_shows_the_destination; ::an_embedded_document_opens_beside_the_one_holding_it; pdf-model/tests/actions.rs::a_root_that_arrives_resumes_the_path_where_it_stopped and ::a_root_named_by_url_is_resolved_against_the_documents_base. The existing end-to-end geometry check is B23 and fails for destination view propagation.
features.verdict: Name-tree child, remote root supply, nested named-child path, no-T root target and window preference have distinct controls. B23 remains a separate current view-loss gap. No filesystem/network behavior beyond the existing host request boundary is demanded here.
features.residuals: No public end-to-end assertion for the Table205 annotation-attachment child selector (/P plus /A) was found; only the model action unit test verifies both integer and named forms. Draft adds a no-F same-root path using an exact-xref root/child fixture. The parser's fixed nesting bound is a resource limit, not an unbounded-support finding.

features.clause: 12.6.4.4, Table 205 and immediately preceding path/cycle prose
features.obligations: R required and P/C. N required only for C child in EmbeddedFiles name tree and absent otherwise. P and A required only for C child attached to a file attachment annotation and absent otherwise; P is zero-based page integer or named destination; A is zero-based annotation index or annotation NM text. T optionally nests next step; absent T means current document is final target. Cyclic target dictionaries are an error and processor should attempt to detect/refuse.
features.assertions: pdf-model action unit tests ::the_clauses_three_example_relationships_read_as_paths and ::a_child_may_be_named_by_the_annotation_it_is_attached_to distinguish paths and all integer/string P/A representations. embedded_go_to.rs public traversal tests exercise N-child and root traversal, but not parent-relative navigation from an already-open embedded source nor P/A attachment route.
features.verdict: N route and nested child target are supported. The current GoToE path state is built from the action's /T chain and `walk` can pop only a child descended during that same action; viewer `jump_into` creates `Open::around(opened)` without retaining its container. Consequently, a subsequent valid GoToE from a child this viewer reached from a parent with `/T << /R /P >>` has no parent context and is declined. Source permits an embedded source and defines /P relative to its actual parent. This is a bounded implementation support gap for known same-root ancestry; independently opening an arbitrary PDF still gives no basis to invent a parent.
features.residuals: The integer P/A route has no public viewer assertion; only the model action unit test currently checks parsed values. The second draft follows the real annotation/FS/EF route and asserts target page 1. Existing `embedded_go_to.rs` named-child route is the N-path positive implementation control. The separate parent-ascent candidate tests a child source with /R /P after actual root→child navigation; parent is correcting version-dependent fixture obligations and complete-chain guards. Cycle refusal is not asserted; MAX_TARGET_DEPTH bounds parse cost but exact cycle refusal needs careful hierarchy fixtures.

Latest observed run is eleven-crate-wave111. Local GoTo control passes. No duplicate B23 created.

reconciliations.2038-B32: Page-label search bound, unrelated to action target traversal; no overlap.

selected_adrs: ADR 1227 governs a different-root /F host request boundary; it does not bar parent ascent through the already-open root's embedded bytes. ADR 0076 governs listing/extraction and does not bar reading an embedded stream for GoToE. ADR 0094 correctly refuses /R /P from a user-opened root, but its sibling-path implementation only remembers documents descended in one action and never supplies ancestry for a child opened on the prior action; the child-origin example is therefore not exercised by the viewer. ADRs 1263/1264 govern window preferences. B23 does not challenge file resolution policy.
bounded_review: Three tables read cell-by-cell with source table headers/continuations and primary annotations. Table 202 and destination-array centering are context only. No blanket signature of all GoTo, GoToR/GoToE destination combinations, host policy, cycles, or malformed input.
